content: A pelvic examination, also referred to as a pelvic exam, is a physical assessment of the female pelvic organs. This examination is generally divided into two components: the external examination and the internal examination. In certain situations, the presence of a chaperone is considered appropriate. The external examination involves the inspection of the external anatomy, including the evaluation of the skin for any lesions or abnormalities. The internal examination requires the use of a speculum to visualize the external cervical os. Additionally, this part of the examination includes an assessment for the presence of any foreign bodies.
